newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jupe rules out reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: France's Jupe rules out reshuffle.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Monday dismissed calls for a cabinet reshuffle or a change in government policies.
"I do not see the need for a cabinet reshuffle. The government is working well," he told France Inter radio in an interview.

Some politicians in the ruling centre-right coalition have called on Gaullist Juppe to bring into his cabinet more centrists and allies of former prime minister Edouard Balladur, who was defeated by fellow-Gaullist Jacques Chirac in the 1995 presidential election.
Juppe said the calls came from some political circles and left the French people rather indifferent. He said the dispute between Chirac and Balladur was a thing of the past.
He also ruled out modifying economic policies despite widespread discontent at austerity, saying his policy was beginning to be successful with a slight decrease in unemployment figures in December.
"We are not going to modify our policy at the time when it seems to be having good results...and business bosses are recovering good morale," he said.
